Impact PDFs, searched areas and acoustic hypotheses

Paired maps use the broadest completed cruise ensemble: 1.02 million initial candidates, with up to 16 turn, 8 Mach and 8 altitude command starts. Their difference is the added drift condition. These remain provisional model-conditioned distributions.

For legibility, the retained impact weights are displayed with a 25 km Gaussian smoothing scale on a 5 km equal-area grid; the original weights are unchanged and exported alongside the display grid. Separate regions are retained where the distribution has separate peaks.

The seventh arc is a reference curve at 40,000 ft; modeled impacts are at sea level. The drift map includes nine recoveries, isotope compatibility and Australian coastal debris non-recovery; acoustic targets and seabed-search outlines do not change either PDF.

Reference: Kadri, U. (2024). Underwater acoustic analysis reveals unique pressure signals associated with aircraft crashes in the sea: revisiting MH370. Scientific Reports, 14, 10102. DOI: 10.1038/s41598-024-60529-1. Page numbers refer to the published PDF; Figure 9 is on p. 9 and Table 1 on p. 14.

All times are UTC on 8 March 2014. Map arrivals are rounded to the nearest second; the table retains the reported or picked timestamps. Impact-time ranges are recalculated at the exact mapped points using effective acoustic speeds of 1.43–1.57 km/s. For E/F, both arrival windows must admit the same impact time, with each propagation path allowed a speed within that range. These are conditional scenario bounds, not confidence intervals; bearing, location and additional propagation errors are not integrated. No unobserved second-station arrival is labelled as a detection.

A/B are entries in Kadri (2024), Table 1 (p. 14), without corresponding peaks recovered by our analysis of the publication trace. D is the candidate marked in Kadri (2024), Fig. 9(c), rectangle 2 (p. 9), with its time and bearing in Table 1 (p. 14). E/F are our exploratory timing constructions from the Fig. 9(c, e) traces, with periodic interference; they are not source locations reported by Kadri (2024). C has no plotted location because its 57° bearing misses the southern arc. This is the earlier discussion shortlist, not a ranking of crash probabilities.

Actual candidate routes after 18:25

Assumptions, search coverage and reproducibility
  • Broad cruise source: 1,020,000 initial candidates, caps 16 turn/8 Mach/8 altitude starts after 18:25; stated mode/frequency and fuel priors remain.
  • The paired maps differ only by the supplied CMEMS nine-recovery, isotope and Australian coastal non-recovery compatibility factors. Gain and acoustic evidence are not multiplied into them.
  • Seventh arc is the archived official FL400 reference; impact altitude is sea level. No impact is forced onto that reference curve.
  • Historical 2014–17 survey data extents, Bluefin display footprints and approximate 2018 outline are shown as context. Proposed renewed-search bands and AIS tracks are not labelled as searched seabed.
  • No calibrated searched-area non-detection likelihood is applied. Current campaign swath completion is not known from these outlines.
  • Kadri target coordinates are conditional geometric constructions. A/B are catalogue entries without recovered corresponding peaks in the published trace. C is unlocalised on the southern arc. D is the preferred reported candidate. E/F are exploratory timing pairs with periodic interference.
  • These model-conditioned impact PDFs remain numerically and physically provisional.

For each mapped target and selected flight/contact model, show the highest-flight-weight retained route within 150 km and the closest retained geographic neighbour. Same endpoint choices are deduplicated in drawings. These are illustrative selections among 213 retained exact histories, not samples from an acoustic-conditioned posterior. Report actual distances and contact weights; geographical proximity alone does not establish a satellite or acoustic match.

PDF, SVG and PNG versions, full-precision impact weights and summary.json accompany this page.
